content.value_statement: Inconsistent CSS makes interfaces hard to theme, maintain, and audit. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code toward structured shadcn-style patterns.
actual_capabilities: Provides HSL color variable patterns for light and dark themes.
Defines spacing, radius, shadow, typography, transition, and z-index scales.
Gives reusable CSS and SCSS patterns for buttons, inputs, cards, badges, and alerts.
Encourages accessible focus states, reduced motion support, and screen reader utilities.
Documents before-and-after examples that replace hard-coded styling with theme tokens.
Supports styling guidance for React, Vue, Blazor, and general web interfaces.
limitations: It is guidance-only and does not install shadcn/ui components.
It does not verify browser rendering or visual regressions automatically.
It does not generate project-specific tokens without user design requirements.
It may need adaptation for existing design systems with different naming rules.

use_cases.title: Refine Existing Component Styles
use_cases.description: Convert hard-coded colors, spacing, and shadows into maintainable theme tokens.

use_cases.title: Build A Theme Foundation
use_cases.description: Create a consistent color, spacing, radius, shadow, and typography system for a product UI.

use_cases.title: Improve Accessibility Defaults
use_cases.description: Add focus-visible states, reduced motion support, high contrast handling, and screen reader utilities.

prompt_templates.title: Style A Basic Component
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the shadcn-aesthetic skill to style this component with CSS variables, accessible focus states, and dark mode support.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor Legacy CSS
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this CSS using shadcn-style tokens for colors, spacing, radius, shadows, and transitions. Preserve the current behavior.

prompt_templates.title: Create A Component Set
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced generation of related UI patterns.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design CSS for buttons, inputs, cards, badges, and alerts using one shared token system and accessible interaction states.

prompt_templates.title: Audit A Design System
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this stylesheet for shadcn-style consistency. Identify hard-coded values, missing accessibility states, and token gaps.

output_examples.input: A plain button uses random padding, a blue hex color, and no keyboard focus style.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends theme tokens for color and spacing, a subtle shadow, hover behavior, and a focus-visible ring.

output_examples.input: A card layout uses margins between items and fixed light-mode colors.
output_examples.output: The skill suggests grid or flex gap, background and border tokens, dark mode variables, and layered shadows.

output_examples.input: A form needs modern input styling with validation states.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines token-based borders, placeholder color, disabled state, focus treatment, and error state styling.

best_practices: Provide the existing CSS and the design intent before asking for refactoring.
Ask for token names that match your project conventions.
Review generated focus, contrast, and motion behavior before shipping.
anti_patterns: Do not request only a visual rewrite without accessibility requirements.
Do not mix hard-coded colors with token-based theme rules.
Do not assume the generated styles match your brand without review.

faq.question: Does this skill install shadcn/ui?
faq.answer: No. It provides CSS and SCSS guidance inspired by shadcn/ui design principles.

faq.question: Can it work outside React?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance applies to CSS and SCSS for React, Vue, Blazor, and general web projects.

faq.question: Does it include dark mode patterns?
faq.answer: Yes. It documents light and dark theme variables and component styles that adapt to those variables.

faq.question: Will it check visual output automatically?
faq.answer: No. You still need browser testing, screenshots, or visual regression checks.

faq.question: Is it useful for design systems?
faq.answer: Yes. It defines shared scales for color, spacing, radius, shadows, typography, transitions, and z-index.

faq.question: Can Codex use this skill?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
